new_entities.name: Pre-exercise caffeine intake
new_entities.description: Caffeine consumed before resistance exercise in ergogenic doses.

new_entities.name: Muscular endurance
new_entities.description: Capacity to sustain repeated resistance-exercise repetitions before fatigue.

edges.effect_quant: Acute caffeine before lifting consistently improves repetition-based resistance-exercise endurance, with small but reproducible pooled effects.
edges.mechanism: By reducing perceived exertion and central fatigue, caffeine helps people tolerate more repetitions before voluntary stopping point. That makes it especially plausible for set-to-failure or repetition-based endurance tasks, which is exactly where the literature tends to find the cleanest benefit.
edges.summary: The evidence for caffeine on muscular endurance is stronger than a lot of gym folklore but smaller than supplement marketing suggests. Across direct meta-analyses, pre-exercise caffeine reliably improves repetition-based resistance performance, usually by a modest margin rather than by a dramatic jump.
edges.caveats: The size of benefit depends on dose, exercise selection, and habitual caffeine exposure. Lower-body endurance effects can be less consistent than upper-body findings in some subgroup analyses.

evidence.citation: Ferreira TT et al 2021 Crit Rev Food Sci Nutr
evidence.notes: Effects of caffeine supplementation on muscle endurance, maximum strength, and perceived exertion in adults submitted to strength training: a systematic review and meta-analyses.
